header.running_head: Hadhrat Umar (RA) Refuses to Accept wealth given to him

blocks.text: when the pangs of death arrive and the chest has tightened"
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) looked at her angrily and said, "O Ummul Mu'mineen! Matters are not like that, but (Allaah states):

blocks.arabic_text: وَجَآءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ ذٰلِكَ مَا كُنْتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيْدُ
blocks.text: The pangs (agony) of death will bring the truth (of Imaan to every person). (It will then be said to the dying person,) "This (death) is what you used to avoid (However, now you have no option)."[^1]

He addressed her further saying, "I had given you an orchard as a gift, but am not satisfied with it. You should therefore return it to my estate." Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) readily agreed and made it over. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, "Since my appointment as Khalifah, I have neither taken a Dinaar or a Dirham of the Muslims. We have of course eaten from their coarse food to fill our bellies and worn their coarse cloth on our backs. Besides that we have none of their spoils apart from this Abyssinian slave, this camel for drawing water and this worn woollen shawl. When I die, I want you to send these items to Hadhrat Umar (RA), thereby alleviating me from being responsible for them."

(After Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) passed away) Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) did as her father had requested. When the messenger came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) (to bring him the items), he wept so profusely that his tears fell on the ground. He said, "May Allaah shower His mercy on Abu Bakr (RA). He has certainly exhausted those to come after him. May Allaah shower His mercy on Abu Bakr (RA). He has certainly exhausted those to come after him." He then commanded his slave to receive all the items. Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) then remarked, "Subhaanallaah! Are you snatching away from Abu Bakr (RA)'s family their Abyssinian slave, their watering camel and their worn woollen shawl worth only five Dirhams?" "What do you advise?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) advised Hadhrat Umar (RA) to give the items back to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)'s family. Hadhrat Umar (RA) however disagreed and said, "No! I swear by the Being Who has sent Muhammad ﷺ with the truth that this shall never happen during my term of Khilaafah. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) would not have escaped from his responsibility for them if I return them to his family and death is ever close by (what will I tell him when I meet him after death?)."[^2]

The Incident of Hadhrat Umar (RA) with Rasulullaah ﷺ
Hadhrat Ataa bin Yasaar reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent a gift to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he returned it. "Why have you returned it?" Rasulullaah
